articles.title: Variety’s Doc Dreams Live Returns to New York for Third Year
articles.summary: Variety is proud to announce the return of Doc Dreams NYC Live, its marquee event dedicated to honoring the art of documentary filmmaking, on Nov. 9 in New York City. Following a successful debut in 2024, Doc Dreams will once again bring together acclaimed filmmakers, storytellers and thought…
body: This year’s 2026 edition of Doc Dreams will continue that tradition, convening some of the industry’s most exciting documentary voices. Alex Gibney, director, writer, and producer of “Musk,” will discuss the documentary’s unvarnished analysis of Elon Musk in a keynote conversation with Variety’s Co-Editor-in-Chief and Co-President Ramin Setoodeh.

The full program of speakers and panels will be announced in the coming weeks, but attendees can expect a dynamic day that celebrates creativity, truth-telling and the impact of nonfiction storytelling in today’s media landscape. Request an invite here: variety.com/docdreams26.

articles.summary: The 19th annual Hamptons Doc Fest has announced its full lineup of 40 films, which includes “Union Town,” “Wild Inside” and “Nuisance Bear.” Running Dec. 3 to Dec. 11, the festival highlights the best non-fiction programming and will open with Barry Avrich’s “Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been,”…
body: Luca Guadagnino’s “Artificial” is set to receive the SF Honors Award, which recognizes bold and innovative filmmaking.

Guadagnino and stars Andrew Garfield, Yura Borisov and Monica Barbaro will accept the award Nov. 17 at the Bay Area Premiere, where they will also join for a post-screening conversation in the Kanbar Hall theater at the Jewish Community Center of San Francisco.

“When SF Honors launched in 2016, the goal was to give Bay Area audiences a front-row seat to the boldest filmmaking of the year,” said SFFILM Board President Todd Traina. “A decade later, I’m thrilled that SF Honors will continue for another five years, and there’s no better film to celebrate that commitment than Artificial. This is a story San Francisco is living through in real time, and Luca Guadagnino’s unique vision and style, together with his impeccable cast, give hometown audiences a new way to see it.”
“Omi,” which will premiere at the Austin Film Festival on Oct. 30, features Bunny Levine in her final film appearance.

articles.title: ‘Harry Potter’ Actor Paapa Essiedu ‘Wouldn’t Have Taken This Job On’ If He Couldn’t Handle Snape Casting Backlash: ‘My Priority Is the Work’
articles.summary: When HBO released the first-look image of Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape in the upcoming “Harry Potter” series, it became immediately clear that the show was going for something different.
body: Essiedu was honored as one of Time’s 100 rising stars defining the next generation of leadership in business, entertainment, sports, politics, and more in New York City. The actor made a name for himself in the U.K. after becoming the first Black actor to play Hamlet for the Royal Shakespeare Company in 2016, winning the Ian Charleson Award, and subsequently earning two BAFTA nominations for his performances in “I May Destroy You” and “The Lazarus Project.” The “Harry Potter” TV series, which Warner Bros. execs are touting as the “streaming event of the decade,” could be the project that catapults the award-winning actor to international stardom.

“I’m really proud of what I’ve seen so far,” he said. “There are so many people who worked so hard on this project — and who it means so much to. It’s been a long time coming. It’s been a long time that people have been saying a lot of things, and now’s the time for people to engage with what we made.”
“Harry Potter” Season 1, based on “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone,” will debut on HBO Max Dec. 25.

body: “This year’s Virtuosos are a powerhouse group from the most talked-about films of the season. I think it’s especially fitting that so many of them are international performers, and I can’t wait to help welcome them all to Santa Barbara,” Turner Classic Movies host and SBIFF moderator Dave Karger said.

Coon will be honored for her role in “The Liberation”; Mariana di Girolamo for “Wild Horse Nine”; Rosalind Eleazar for “Misty Green”; Jordan Firstman for “Club Kid”; Anthony Ippolito for “I Play Rocky”; Jaafar Jackson for “Michael”; Inde Navarrette for “Obsession”; Kate O’Flynn for “Tender Loving Care.”
Honorees over the last six years include Jacob Elordi, Chase Infiniti, Zendaya, Sydney Sweeney, Andrew Scott, Austin Butler, Renate Reinsve, Kieran Culkin, Harris Dickinson and many more.

articles.title: Sir Patrick Stewart remembered as 'Mirfield's finest'
articles.summary: Tributes have been paid to the legendary Star Trek actor Sir Patrick Stewart, who was born in Mirfield.
body: Sir Patrick Stewart once said he had to drop his Yorkshire accent for Hollywood, but he never forgot his roots.

The Mirfield-born actor, best known for his roles in Star Trek and the X-Men films, died at the age of 86 at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday after suffering with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
His death has prompted an outpouring of love from the community he proudly called home, along with his beloved Huddersfield Town - the club he followed from childhood.
Stewart's friend and fellow legendary actor Sir Ian McKellen said Stewart "never forsook his origins".

articles.title: Russell Brand accusers 'haunted' for years by alleged crimes, court hears
articles.summary: The women involved in the case had "nothing to gain" apart from "some closure", the prosecutor says.
body: Some of the women in Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault case have been "haunted" for years by what they allege he did to them, jurors have been told.
In her closing speech at London's Southwark Crown Court on Friday, prosecutor Reil Karmy-Jones KC said the women had "nothing to gain" from coming forward apart from "some closure".
Speaking for the defence, Polly Dyer told jurors Brand had pleaded guilty and been fined over possession of cannabis in 1995, but had no other "convictions, cautions, reprimands or warnings".
Brand, 51, is on trial facing seven charges; three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of attempted indecent assault. He denies the charges.

articles.title: Oh to Believe in Another World review – William Kentridge’s amazing animated ballet of black comic pain
articles.summary: Kentridge’s cine-musical creation, made to accompany Shostakovich’s 10th Symphony, is a marvel of puppetry, dance and humour, exploring humanity, grief and idealism. The Baku international arts festival in Azerbaijan is showcasing an amazing cine-musical creation, perhaps the most amazing animation…
body: My colleague Jonathan Jones has written about Kentridge’s film but what I hadn’t anticipated was how funny it is: the simple, preposterous effect of seeing Stalin’s great big monumental face on top of a dancer’s body, and seeing that face remain unchanged despite the exertions below, staring resolutely ahead at the far horizon of history. It is hilarious, a little like Terry Gilliam’s animations for Monty Python. But is it supposed to be funny? Chaplin showed that the way to defy Hitler was to laugh at him. Kentridge (and Kentridge’s Shostakovich) are doing something similar with Stalin but not exactly the same. It is a ballet of black comic pain.

articles.title: Sir Ian McKellen leads tributes to 'beloved actor' Sir Patrick Stewart after his death at 86
articles.summary: The actor died in Los Angeles following a "a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
body: Sir Ian McKellen has led tributes to Sir Patrick Stewart following his death at the age of 86, calling him "the most respected and beloved actor of his generation".
"He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love," Sir Ian, Sir Patrick's X-Men co-star, said.
Famous for his role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek, Sir Patrick was a versatile actor who won multiple awards, balancing Hollywood roles and a career in classical theatre.
William Shatner, who also helmed the USS Enterprise in Star Trek, said Sir Patrick brought "intelligence, grace and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did".

articles.title: Footage of Seoul crush to be removed from Call of Duty after backlash
articles.summary: Bereaved families say they were appalled to see footage of the Itaewon disaster included in Modern Warfare 4.
body: Video clips showing the aftermath of a deadly crush in Seoul will be removed from the latest Call of Duty game after an angry reaction from victims' families.
Real life news coverage of the 2022 disaster which killed almost 160 people was included in an opening scene of Modern Warfare 4 to illustrate a fictional invasion from North Korea.
Bereaved families said they were "appalled" to see the footage - which included people being removed on stretchers, body bags on the street and resuscitation efforts - repurposed for the game.
Activision, which makes Call of Duty, has since apologised and confirmed it would be removed in the game's next update on 12 November.
